items.text: On Ward 6B, does a structured bedside handoff checklist with a medicines section, tested in PDSA cycles from October to December 2026, reduce the weekly proportion of nursing handoffs with at least one missed medication reconciliation item from about 38 percent to 20 percent or less?
items.population: Nursing shift handoffs at 07:00 and 19:00 for adult inpatients on Ward 6B
items.intervention: Structured bedside handoff checklist with a four-line medicines section and fortnightly feedback at the huddle
items.comparator: Eight-week baseline of the current verbal station handoff
items.outcome: Weekly proportion of handoffs with at least one missed reconciliation item on handoff sheet review against the medication administration record
items.time: Eight baseline weeks, then 12 weeks of PDSA cycles

finer: Feasible within approved huddle time and existing sheets; interesting to nursing and pharmacy; novel only locally, which suits QI; ethical under the QI screening determination; relevant because of two recent near misses.
summary: One SMART QI aim with a time-bound target and a run-chart outcome.
